newsitem.title: GERMANY: German direct marketing agencies see 10 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: German direct marketing agencies see 10 pct growth.

text.p: The German direct marketing association (DDV) said on Monday its agencies boosted turnover by an average of 10 percent last year, largely driven by business from financial services companies.

Direct marketing budgets of financial services have increased in Germany for the last two years, and last year this coincided with more investment by media companies and brand-name consumer product manufacturers.
"In addition to financial services, new media online services and telecommunications companies were also listed as driving forces behind the continuing growth," DDV spokesman Holger Albers said.
"Companies which manufacture brand-name products have also continued to discover direct marketing as a strategic instrument in their marketing mix," Albers said.

The DDV recently released projections for the current year which foresaw a 10 percent jump in direct marketing spending this year to 33 billion marks ($19.1 billion). It said half of all advertising money spent in Germany goes toward direct marketing.
The DDV listed BBDO, Wunderman Cato Johnson and Ogilvy & Mather Direkt GmbH as the three largest direct marketing agencies in Germany.
The DDV comprises 740 members including telephone marketing companies, mailing list distributors and media companies which carry direct-marketing advertising. ($ = 1.726 German Marks)
